to.notes: Pause clients for `timeout` milliseconds, until it expires or `CLIENT UNPAUSE`. `ALL` (the default) holds every command but `CLIENT UNPAUSE`; `WRITE` holds anything that may write — writes, `PFCOUNT`, `PUBLISH`, scripts not declared `no-writes`, and an `EXEC` containing any of them. A pause given during another keeps the more restrictive of the two. While writes are paused nothing expires, as in Redis: a read takes a key whose time has passed as gone, but it is deleted, counted in `expired_keys` and announced only once the pause is over, and `RANDOMKEY` may name it rather than answer nil. The same holds during a slot handoff and a manual failover

from.notes: All or nothing: an unknown parameter, a value out of range, a parameter that cannot change at run time or one named twice is an error naming it, and none of the pairs is applied. `requirepass`, `slowlog-log-slower-than`, `slowlog-max-len`, `maxmemory`, `maxmemory-policy`, `maxmemory-samples`, `lfu-log-factor`, `lfu-decay-time`, `appendonly`, `loglevel`, `repl-backlog-size`, `repl-backlog-ttl`, `repl-diskless-load` all apply immediately at runtime without restart

from.notes: Return server info; sections include `server`, `keyspace`, `replication`, `errorstats` (per-error reply counters), `all`, etc. `INFO commandstats` has, for each command that has been called, `calls`, `usec`, `usec_per_call`, `rejected_calls` and `failed_calls`, and the Redis 8.8 slowlog fields `slowlog_count`, `slowlog_time_ms_sum` and `slowlog_time_ms_max`. `INFO memory` reports `used_memory` (allocated bytes — what `maxmemory` is compared with), `used_memory_rss` and `maxmemory_policy`; `INFO stats` reports `evicted_keys`
